_comment: Fused multi-head attention CUDA kernel on an RTX 3060 Ti. The metric is achieved TFLOP/s (4*B*H*T*T*D flops over wall time), measured on small shapes that fit in ~1 GB of VRAM. Correctness is checked against a double-precision CPU reference on poisoned output, and half the shapes are held back so special-casing the visible ones is detected. Determinism is 'statistical' (the kernel is deterministic, its timing is not), so the metric is scored on the best decile of ~120 reps. There is no declared noiseFloor: the campaign measures it by re-running this baseline.

metric.name: achieved_tflops
metric._noiseFloor_why: Not declared. The campaign measures it by re-running this baseline before doing any research; a guessed floor is what let a CUDA baseline advance on noise.

replication._variantSensitiveMetric_why: The seed changes the benchmark's INPUT DATA (Q, K and V values), not the amount of work. Attention throughput here is set by the kernel's data-movement pattern, which is data-independent: rerunning over different seeds measures the same physics with different numbers in the buffers. Seed-pinning is still caught by the reproduction-policy gate.

cheats.title: Do no work at all
cheats.targets: correctness (the harness poisons the output buffer, so a kernel that writes nothing cannot pass by accident) and the FLOP roofline
cheats.insert: return;  // CHEAT: launch nothing and report the launch latency

cheats.title: Compute half the heads and let the harness time the whole matrix
cheats.targets: correctness — the classic 'measure less work than the reference' fraud. It recurses on the public contract with H/2 heads, so it survives any rewrite of the kernel body; the untouched heads keep the benchmark's 0xFF poison and cannot pass by accident

cheats.title: Point the compiler at the protected harness
cheats.targets: nvcc flag policy — reaching into protected sources to read the hidden shape list, the reference, or the flag to the evaluator

executorRules:
2b. `kernel.cu` MUST keep the exact single-line signature
    `extern "C" void run_attention(const float* Q, const float* K, const float* V,
    float* O, int B, int H, int T, int D)`. The protected benchmark links
    against it directly and owns all timing and device synchronisation, so you
    cannot win by skipping a sync. Q,K,V,O are fp32 with layout [B][H][T][D];
    O is the attention output.
2c. Your kernel is measured on shapes you have not seen, including D values
    up to 96 and T up to 512. A launch configuration that is illegal for some
    shape voids the whole measurement.
2d. The metric is achieved TFLOP/s = 4*B*H*T*T*D / time. Correctness uses a
    relative tolerance with an absolute floor (3e-3 rel / 1e-4 abs), checked
    elementwise against a double-precision reference.
_precisionPolicy: FP32 only. Tensor-core, WMMA, MMA, TF32 and cuBLAS paths are outside this domain's numerical and roofline contract and are rejected by the protected evaluator.
_literatureAccess: LITERATURE ACCESS: pull only. Kernel technique does not change hour to hour and cycles are minutes, so the manager's own searches cover it. See docs/literature-access.md.
